query: According to episode 7, why can no machine decide in general whether an arbitrary program halts?
answer: Turing showed that the idea of a “checker” – a machine that could take any program (and its input) and always tell, in finite time, whether that program will eventually stop – leads to a logical contradiction. By assuming such a checker existed and then using it in a self‑referential construction (the same trick as the liar’s paradox), he proved the assumption collapses. Because that contradiction is airtight, no mechanical procedure can ever work for every possible program. In other words, the halting problem is undecidable: no machine can decide in general whether an arbitrary program halts. (Episode 7, 26:22‑27:51; also see the description of the checker and the proof‑by‑contradiction argument in Episode 7, 23:24‑24:54.)
